original_question: Two groups G1 and G2 are said to be commensurable if there exist finiteindex subgroups H1 ⩽ G1 and H2 ⩽ G2(not necessarily of the same index) such that H1 ∼= H2. Let A[F4 ] and A[H4 ] denote the Artin groups of spherical types F4 and H4, respectively. Are these two groups commensurable? This is the most difficult case in the classification of Artin groups of spherical type up to commensurability.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 21.128 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": whether the spherical-type Artin groups A[F4] and A[H4] are commensurable.
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper's official formulation essentially verbatim: it states the paper's definition of commensurability, identifies A[F4] and A[H4] as the Artin groups of spherical types F4 and H4, asks exactly whether these two groups are commensurable, and preserves the paper's contextual note that this is the most difficult remaining case in the commensurability classification for Artin groups of spherical type.
refined_question: Let A[F4] and A[H4] denote the Artin groups associated to the spherical Coxeter types F4 and H4, respectively. Are A[F4] and A[H4] commensurable; that is, do there exist finite-index subgroups H_F <= A[F4] and H_H <= A[H4] such that H_F is isomorphic to H_H?
justification: For the arXiv item actually specified here, the relevant target is not a numbered conjecture or theorem from a standard research article, but the Kourovka Notebook open problem 21.128. The draft reproduces that problem almost exactly. The refinement therefore stays completely narrow: it keeps the same two Artin groups, the same notion of commensurability, and the same scope, while rewriting the statement as one self-contained research question with the definition folded into the sentence.
